The Magna Carta, signed in 1215, was a significant document that laid the foundation for modern democracy and the rule of law. It established the principle that everyone, including the king, was subject to the law and that no one was above the law. The Magna Carta also protected individual rights and limited the power of the monarchy, which helped to establish the concept of constitutional government. Its principles have influenced many other countries and continue to be relevant today. In short, the Magna Carta is a landmark document that played a crucial role in shaping the development of democratic societies.
